title: Heap buffer overflow via input-controlled copy length in parse_alpha
rationale: Root cause: entry.c:23 assigns claimed from untrusted input with no upper bound, and entry.c:27 passes it directly as the memcpy length into an 8-byte heap allocation. The fix clamps claimed to the allocation size (8) and to the available source bytes (len - 1) immediately after the allocation null-check, before the memcpy.
variants_checked: entry.c:parse_bravo -- uses memcpy(name, buf, len) with the caller-supplied len, not an embedded length field. Different bug class (stack-buffer-overflow), different root cause pattern. Not addressed by this fix. entry.c:parse_charlie -- no memcpy; UAF bug, unrelated pattern.
bypass_considered: An attacker sets buf[0] = 255 (claimed = 255). The first clamp reduces it to 8. The attacker then provides exactly 2 bytes of input (len = 2, so len - 1 = 1). The second clamp reduces claimed to 1. The memcpy writes 1 byte into the 8-byte buffer -- safe.
test_note: No regression test added. The canary target has no C test harness or test directory.
review_reason: The diff is confined to parse_alpha, the only function on the path to the vulnerable memcpy at line 27. It fixes the root cause by clamping claimed to both the allocation size (8) and the available input length (len - 1) before the copy. No new parsing or trust boundaries are introduced. The fix is minimal, idiomatic C, and matches the surrounding literal-constant style.
